paper.title: Optimizer Choice Matters For The Emergence of Neural Collapse

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-5 and Appendices B (NC metrics), D (setup, hyperparameters, NC0-NC3 regression, ablations on epochs, UFM, momentum, zero weight decay, other datasets, ImageNet, ViT); C (related work) and E (proofs) skimmed

claims.claim: Whether neural collapse (the last-layer features and classifier weights settling into a symmetric simplex configuration late in training) emerges depends on how the optimizer applies weight decay: adaptive optimizers that add weight decay to the gradient (Adam, Signum) produce it, while the same optimizers with decoupled weight decay (AdamW, SignumW) do not, even at far larger weight decay. Supported only if, across ResNet9 and VGG9 on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 over a grid of learning rates, momenta and weight decays, the decoupled variants end with higher NC0 (squared row sum of the last-layer weights, which must vanish under collapse) and NC3 than the coupled variants at every weight decay; if in the reference setting AdamW's NC0 ends above its initial value while Adam's falls by at least 80% and AdamW reduces NC3 by under 50% against at least 75% for Adam; if shifting weight decay from the decoupled to the coupled form at fixed total strength lowers NC0 and NC3 steadily without changing validation accuracy; and if Adam versus AdamW on ResNet50 / ImageNet shows the same gap.
claims.decision_rule: AdamW/SignumW NC0 and NC3 > Adam/Signum at all WD (36 settings); reference run AdamW NC0 > init, Adam NC0 <= -80%; NC3 AdamW > -50% vs Adam <= -75%; coupled-fraction sweep monotone with flat val acc; ImageNet ResNet50 AdamW without full NC.

claims.claim: In finite training, weight decay is needed for neural collapse and momentum speeds collapse beyond what it does for the training loss, as predicted by the fact that under SGD the last-layer row sum shrinks at an exponential rate set by weight decay and momentum. Supported only if SGD without weight decay, even after 2,000 epochs, ends with collapse metrics several times larger than SGD with weight decay after 200 epochs; if two SGD runs differing only in momentum reach the same training loss but clearly different collapse metrics; and if the NC0 metric explains at least 70% of the variance in NC3 across converged runs.
claims.decision_rule: No-WD SGD at 2,000 epochs NC1/NC2/NC3 >= 2x WD SGD at 200 epochs; mom 0.7 vs 0.9 same train loss, different NC; regression R^2(NC3 ~ NC0) >= 0.70.

experiments.text: Define the grid and metrics. Setup: ResNet9 and VGG9 on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 with SGD, SGDW, Adam, AdamW, Signum and SignumW; three learning rates, six momenta and six weight decays each (3,888 runs, about 2,500 kept after discarding runs that failed to train), 200 epochs, batch 128, step decay by 10x at one and two thirds. Metrics: NC1 (within-class variability), NC2 (class means and weights form a simplex), NC3 (self-duality of weights and means), and the new NC0 = squared norm of the last-layer weights' row sum, which must reach zero for collapse (necessary, not sufficient); NC4 is dropped because it holds whenever training accuracy nears 100%. Collapse strength is judged relative to initial values and to the best values seen.

Compare coupled and decoupled weight decay. Setup: final metrics across weight decays (averaged over learning rates and momenta) and full trajectories on ResNet9 / FashionMNIST. Result: in the reference run NC0 / NC1 / NC2 / NC3 end at 2.1e-4 / 0.05 / 0.29 / 0.35 for SGD, 0.55 / 0.26 / 0.46 / 0.80 for SGDW, 0.34 / 0.04 / 0.29 / 0.29 for Adam (NC0 -80.6%, NC3 -79.5%), 5.33 / 0.20 / 0.54 / 0.78 for AdamW (NC0 far above initial, NC3 -45.2%), 0.78 / 0.13 / 0.50 / 0.58 for Signum and 3,186 / 0.30 / 1.15 / 1.40 for SignumW. AdamW and SignumW stay above Adam and Signum on NC0 and NC3 even with weight decay orders of magnitude larger; the smallest singular value of the last-layer weights grows under AdamW and SignumW. The pattern repeats on the other architecture-dataset pairs and on ResNet50 / ImageNet (Adam vs AdamW, 90 epochs).

Interpolate between Adam and AdamW. Setup: ResNet9 / MNIST, momentum 0.9, total weight decay fixed at 0.0005 split between a coupled and a decoupled part. Result: moving weight decay into the coupled part steadily lowers NC0, NC2 and NC3 while validation accuracy stays essentially the same, so collapse and generalisation come apart. Theory on sign gradient descent (Adam with beta1 = beta2 = 0) in the unconstrained-feature model: with decoupled decay NC0 rises monotonically to (K-2)^2 / lambda^2; with coupled decay a decaying learning rate exists that drives it to zero; a small MLP experiment shows the predicted non-monotone versus saturating NC0 curves.

Check partial collapse and the limits of the evidence. Setup: the run with the smallest NC3 and over 99% training accuracy per optimizer; preliminary ViT runs on CIFAR-10. Result: in its best run AdamW reaches the lowest NC1 (0.01) and NC2 (0.14) of all optimizers while NC0 is 8.09 and NC3 0.49 (Adam 0.12 / 0.04 / 0.23 / 0.17; SGDW 1.5e-4 / 0.01 / 0.15 / 0.10), so collapse properties do not always appear together and SGDW can collapse fully. In ViTs NC0 first rises then falls for both Adam and AdamW and NC3 is U-shaped, with runs kept at only 50% training accuracy. Theory covers only SGD and sign descent on the unconstrained-feature model, and Table 1's summary marks convergence for the decoupled case and none for the coupled case, the reverse of the theorem statements.

Test weight decay and momentum under SGD. Setup: ResNet9 / FashionMNIST; SGD with zero weight decay for 200 and 2,000 epochs at several momenta; heatmaps over momentum and weight decay; two runs with weight decay 0.005 and momentum 0.7 vs 0.9. Result: without weight decay NC1 / NC2 / NC3 stay at about 0.2 / 0.55 / 0.7 after 2,000 epochs, against 0.02 / 0.2 / 0.13 with weight decay after 200 epochs; larger momentum lowers the metrics at fixed non-zero weight decay, increasingly so at larger weight decay; the momentum 0.7 and 0.9 runs reach almost the same training loss but clearly different final collapse metrics. Theorems show NC0 decays exponentially under SGD with coupled or decoupled decay when 0 < lr x wd < 2(1 + momentum) or < 2.

Relate NC0 to the standard metrics and check training length. Setup: regress NC3 on NC0 across converged runs per learning rate and pooled; extend selected runs to 2,000 epochs; normalise NC0 by the weight norm. Result: slope 0.14-0.20 with R^2 0.78-0.84 per learning rate and 0.73 pooled over 399 runs (p < 0.001); NC0 correlates visibly less with NC1 and NC2. Longer training lowers all metrics somewhat but leaves the weight-decay trends unchanged and barely moves AdamW's NC0 and NC3; the normalised NC0 gives the same conclusions except at zero weight decay, where it no longer tracks NC1-NC3.
